quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 3096, 1002, or 3727?
quests.hint: The smallest number is the one you'd reach first while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 3096, 1002, and 3727, the number 1002 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 1002, you get 1003!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the thousands place of 2029?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the thousands spot.
quests.explanation: In 2029, the digit 2 sits in the thousands place!
quests.funFact: Double 2 is 4! Because 2 + 2 = 4.

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 4194 or 3067?
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 4194 is greater than 3067 -- when counting up, 4194 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 4194 by 10, it becomes 41940!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 2659?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the hundreds spot.
quests.explanation: In 2659, the digit 6 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: If you had 6 apples and found one more, you would have 7 apples!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.hint: Sound the word out slowly, then count that many fingers to check.
quests.explanation: "Eight Hundred Sixty-Five" is how we say the number 865 in English, so 865 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: The number 865 is an odd number!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 500, 1500, 2500, 3500, __?
quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 1000, so after 3500 comes 3500 + 1000 = 4500!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 4500 comes right after 4499!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 3957 or 3301?
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 3957 is greater than 3301 -- when counting up, 3957 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 3957 comes just before 3958!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 0, 250, 500, __?
quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 250, so after 500 comes 500 + 250 = 750!
quests.funFact: Double 750 is 1500! Because 750 + 750 = 1500.

quests.instruction: What digit is in the thousands place of 1406?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the thousands digit in 1406.
quests.explanation: In 1406, the digit 1 sits in the thousands place!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 1 comes right after 0!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 500, so after 2000 comes 2000 + 500 = 2500!
quests.funFact: If you had 2500 apples and found one more, you would have 2501 apples!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Read the numeral 4744 out loud -- what word do you say?
quests.explanation: The numeral 4744 is written in words as "Four Thousand Seven Hundred Forty-Four" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: In math, knowing how to read words like 'Four Thousand Seven Hundred Forty-Four' is just as important as knowing the digits!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 3010, 1226, or 1259?
quests.hint: The greatest number is the one you'd reach last while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 3010, 1226, and 1259, the number 3010 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 3010 by 10, it becomes 30100!

quests.instruction: Which number is smaller: 952 or 2569?
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach first is the answer.
quests.explanation: 952 is smaller than 2569 -- when counting up, 952 comes earlier!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 952, it stays exactly the same: 952!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 500, 1500, 2500, 3500, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 1000, so after 3500 comes 3500 + 1000 = 4500!
quests.funFact: The number 4500 is an even number!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.hint: Break the word into parts -- does it sound like a small number, a "teen", or a bigger one?
quests.explanation: "Two Thousand Seven Hundred Nineteen" is how we say the number 2719 in English, so 2719 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 2719 comes right after 2718!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 2368 or 1709?
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 2368 is greater than 1709 -- when counting up, 2368 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 2368 comes just before 2369!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.hint: Break the word into parts -- does it sound like a small number, a "teen", or a bigger one?
quests.explanation: "Two Thousand One Hundred Seventy" is how we say the number 2170 in English, so 2170 is the digit that matches!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 1706?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the tens digit in 1706.
quests.explanation: In 1706, the digit 0 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: Zero is a special even number that comes before 1.

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 500, 1000, 1500, __?
quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 500, so after 1500 comes 1500 + 500 = 2000!
quests.funFact: If you had 2000 apples and found one more, you would have 2001 apples!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 4635?
quests.hint: Split 4635 into its place-value parts, then find the tens part.
quests.explanation: In 4635, the digit 3 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 3 comes just before 4!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Count up to 2926 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 2926 is written in words as "Two Thousand Nine Hundred Twenty-Six" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: When you can read big math words like 'Two Thousand Nine Hundred Twenty-Six', you are becoming a true math master!

quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 2409, 874, or 3655?
quests.hint: The smallest number is the one you'd reach first while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 2409, 874, and 3655, the number 874 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 874, it stays exactly the same: 874!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 2662?
quests.hint: Split 2662 into its place-value parts, then find the ones part.
quests.explanation: In 2662, the digit 2 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 2, you get 3!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 4746 or 3330?
quests.hint: Line the numbers up on a number line in your head -- further right is bigger.
quests.explanation: 4746 is greater than 3330 -- when counting up, 4746 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 4746 comes right after 4745!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 1024, 1949, or 2558?
quests.hint: The greatest number is the one you'd reach last while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 1024, 1949, and 2558, the number 2558 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 2558 comes just before 2559!

quests.instruction: Which number is smaller: 4896 or 1548?
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 1548 is smaller than 4896 -- when counting up, 1548 comes earlier!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 2521?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the hundreds spot.
quests.explanation: In 2521, the digit 5 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: The number 5 is an odd number!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Look at how many digits 1964 has, then think of how that word usually sounds.
quests.explanation: The numeral 1964 is written in words as "One Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty-Four" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: The word 'One Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty-Four' helps us communicate numbers without just drawing shapes!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 3114, 1659, or 3325?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the bigger one.
quests.explanation: Out of 3114, 1659, and 3325, the number 3325 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you had 3325 apples and found one more, you would have 3326 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 1811 or 3007?
quests.hint: Line the numbers up on a number line in your head -- further right is bigger.
quests.explanation: 3007 is greater than 1811 -- when counting up, 3007 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 3007 by 10, it becomes 30070!
